newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HEAVEN SHARES SWEETEN INVESTOR APPETITE.
newsitem.headline: HEAVEN SHARES SWEETEN INVESTOR APPETITE.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Sweets from Heaven Holdings Ltd were gobbled up in heavy trading on Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) as investors responded enthusiastically to an earlier cautionary announcement.
Stocks in the confectionery retail group soared 18 cents or 17 percent to a best ever level of 126 cents in morning trade.

By 1255GMT the shares had slipped off their peaks to 120 cents, but were still eagerly in demand. Almost two million Heaven shares, worth 2.4 million rand, had changed hands, making the stock one of the most actively traded on the JSE on Friday.
"No one is sure what the cautionary is about, but talk on the street is that there might be a tie-up across the water," an equity dealer said.
"When it listed it did say it was looking to get into the U.S. And it is already in Australia," the dealer said.
On Friday, Heaven, which was listed on the JSE in June, cautioned shareholders that it was in talks which could have an impact on its share price. It gave no further details.
A stores analyst who asked not to be identified said there were rumours Heaven may sign a deal with South African retailer CNA Gallo Ltd whereby mini sweet-shops would be set up in CNA stores.
"It would not be a merger or acquisition but rather a deal whereby Heaven pays CNA a certain amount per square metre of store space. Or they could just split the profits," the analyst said.
CNA shares were last trading unchanged at 400 cents after 226,800 units had changed hands.
Heaven, which has also set up shop in Zimbabwe, Mauritius and Namibia, last month bought the franchise and operating assets of Brittan's Sweets for 2.4 million rand.
